outcomes.text: Talk about relationships with family and friends, and marriage or partnership.
Discuss social media and mobile technology in daily life.
Discuss music, cinema and TV, food and eating out, and sport.
Describe customs and festivals in Italian-speaking countries and communities.

topics.title: 3.1.2 Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest

outcomes.text: Describe home, town, neighbourhood and region.
Discuss charity and voluntary work, and healthy and unhealthy living.
Discuss the environment, poverty and homelessness.
Talk about travel and tourism.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Theme 3: Current and future study and employment

outcomes.text: Talk about school subjects and studies.
Describe life at school or college.
Discuss education after 16.
Discuss jobs, career choices and ambitions.
Follow clear standard Italian and identify messages, key points, details and opinions in short and longer passages.
Recognise past, present and future events and deduce meaning from narratives and authentic material.
Answer questions, extract information, evaluate and draw conclusions from extended spoken text.
Hold a short conversation, asking and answering questions and exchanging opinions.
Narrate events and convey information, adapting language for new purposes.
Speak spontaneously, using rephrasing or repair, and develop longer stretches of speech.
Use varied vocabulary and structures across tenses, justify views, and pronounce and intone accurately.
Understand general and specific details in varied texts, including authentic sources and adapted literary extracts.
Identify messages, key points and opinions, scan for information, infer and recognise implicit meaning.
Translate a short passage from Italian into English.
Write short texts with simple accurate sentences to exchange information.
Write extended text giving facts, ideas and opinions across past, present and future, in suitable style and register.
Translate sentences and short texts from English into Italian.
Use noun gender and singular and plural forms, including common irregulars such as la mano and gli uomini.
Use definite, indefinite and partitive articles.
Make adjectives agree and place them correctly.
Form regular comparatives and superlatives and use di and che after comparatives.
Use demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative adjectives.
Form adverbs and their comparatives, and use time and place adverbs, ecco and common adverbial phrases.
Use expressions of quantity such as abbastanza, molto, poco, troppo.
Use subject, direct and indirect object, reflexive and disjunctive pronouns.
Use relative, demonstrative, indefinite and interrogative pronouns, and recognise ci, vi and object pronoun order.
Use regular, irregular and reflexive verbs in all persons, with negative and interrogative forms and tu, voi, Lei.
Use impersonal verbs and verbs followed by an infinitive, with or without a preposition.
Use present, immediate future, perfect (avere and essere) and conditional (vorrei, mi piacerebbe), and imperfect of avere, essere, stare, fare.
Recognise stare + gerund, the future, other imperfects and the pluperfect.
Use negative structures such as non ... mai, non ... più, non ... niente, non ... nessuno, neanche.
Use common and compound prepositions, contracted forms with the article, and da with the present tense.
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions such as e, ma, quando, perché, anche se.
Use ordinal and cardinal numbers, common quantities, time and dates.
Use less common irregular nouns such as il dito, le dita.
Use irregular comparatives and superlatives like il migliore, il peggiore, and quello and bello before nouns.
Use irregular adverb comparatives such as meglio and peggio.
Use ci, ne, combined direct and indirect pronouns, and object pronoun position and order.
Use impersonal si, relative il quale, il cui, possessive and less common indefinite pronouns.
Use dependent infinitives, perfect infinitive after dopo, and impersonal constructions like si dice.
Use stare + gerund, imperfect, future, conditional and pluperfect, recognising future and conditional perfect.
Use the passive voice and the present subjunctive in common expressions, recognising the past subjunctive.
Use da with the imperfect tense.
Ignore unneeded words and use visual and verbal context to infer meaning.
Use layout, title and pictures to predict a text's content.
Use grammatical markers and real-world knowledge to anticipate meaning.
Recognise word-formation patterns such as diminutives, -mente adverbs, ri- and s-/in- prefixes and common suffixes.
Use cognates and near-cognates while watching for false friends like camera and libreria.
Apply Italian-English spelling rules such as -ty to -tà, -ion to -ione, -ct- to -tt-, and -ph- to -f-.
Use a dictionary carefully, checking meaning in context and avoiding word-for-word translation.
Use pointing, expression, gesture, mime and drawing to keep communication going.
Use a similar word, description of properties, or reference to features or function when a word is forgotten.
Ask for help or repetition, simplify, or paraphrase while avoiding word coinage and topic avoidance.
Understand Italian exam instructions such as Completa, Scegli, Rispondi, Descrivi and Menziona.
Use comparison words such as migliore, peggiore, simile, stesso.
Use connectives such as però, quindi, inoltre, purtroppo, soprattutto.
Ask questions and use common question forms.
Use common questions.
Know the alphabet and accents.
Know cardinal numbers to 1,000, ordinals to twenty-first, and approximate numbers like dozzina.
Use greetings and exclamations.
Express opinions.
Use expressions of time.
Describe location and distance.
Name colours.
Use weights and measures.
Describe shapes.
Talk about the weather.
Use access vocabulary.
Use correctness vocabulary.
Name materials.
Use common verbs.
Use impersonal verbs.
Learn foundation vocabulary for family and friends, technology, free time, and customs and festivals.
